topic: the archive reproduces from a fresh cache; bigger DMA chunks are confirmed useless once the L2 policy is set

reproduction.command: the exact command documented in final-status.md, with a brand new empty cache directory

negative_result.hypothesis: reading 8 rows per DMA instead of 4 would raise read throughput (a pure read microbenchmark rises from 0.84 at 8KB to 2.13 TB/s at 128KB)
negative_result.finding: with the L2 policy set, a 32KB copy already reaches 1.757 TB/s and a 64KB copy reaches 1.725 TB/s, i.e. no further benefit from chunk size. The chunk-size curve only matters when the policy is unset.
negative_result.consequence: the last mechanical idea for closing the prefill gap is dropped; it would have cost a large rewrite for no gain

status: decode certified on three independent windows; prefill remains about 20% short
